title: Security and callback boundaries
summary: Browser/API/Observation integrations reuse the common Crypto + Access Control + Permissions + Security Effect architecture rather than inventing local trust models.
invariants: Authentication/cryptographic attribution is evidence, not automatic access or method authority.
Protected session creation, route use, observation subscription and browser control are permissioned operations at their respective seams.
proofRef is evidence linkage, not a bearer capability.
Observation subscriptions are read-side authority and never become universal remote control.
Completion routing uses registered capabilities/session routing rather than arbitrary callback URLs embedded in work requests.
Password/secret values must not be exposed through Observation history.

provenance.claim: Observation explicitly leaves authorization to the common security architecture.
Allocator production authorities remain injected and do not create a second trust/key-management system.
